Former Super Falcons coach Randy Waldrum was appointed head coach of Malawi’s women’s national team on Wednesday ahead of the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil, PUNCH Sports Extra reports. Waldrum signed a two-year contract with Malawi following the team’s run to the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations final. The former Houston Dash and Nigeria women’s coach was unveiled as the replacement for Lovemore Fazili, who will serve as his assistant while reportedly furthering his coaching qualifications. NWSL star Temwa Chawinga and OL Lyonnes’ Tabitha Chawinga were the standout players in a WAFCON campaign in which Malawi defeated Nigeria, Egypt, Ghana and Algeria en route to the final, where they lost 3-0 to Cameroon. Despite the defeat, Malawi secured qualification for next year’s FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. “I watched the games during WAFCON and followed the team very closely,” Waldrum said during his unveiling, according to a statement by the Malawi FA (FAM). I love to control games through possession. “The modern game involves a lot of attacking transitions, and you need that quality in your team. I know that quality is already there with the talent you have.” Oshoala’s super hat-trick sends Al Hilal into Saudi Cup q’finals Super Falcons get $100,000 equivalent as Tinubu fulfils pledge FULL LIST: Last 10 rankings for 2026 Ballon d’Or revealed FAM president Fleetwood Haiya described Waldrum’s appointment, following his stint as Nigeria coach at the 2023 Women’s World Cup, as a step up ahead of next year’s tournament. “This is another important day as we continue to fulfil the commitments of our strategic plan,” Haiya said. “When we took office, we promised Malawians that we would invest in building a sustainable women’s national team and developing women’s football. “The appointment of Coach Randy is part of that commitment. We want to strengthen the technical team and ensure there is a clear pathway for our players, from grassroots to elite football. “I want to recognise Coach Fazili and his technical team for the wonderful job they did at WAFCON and for leading us to the World Cup. “They did a very good job. However, the World Cup is another bigger stage, and we felt it was important to bring in someone with the qualifications and experience of coaching at that level. “Coach Randy brings that experience, qualification and competence.” Waldrum resigned as Super Falcons coach in September 2024, citing family reasons. Before his departure, he had been at loggerheads with the Nigeria Football Federation, accusing the federation of maladministration in the management of the team during preparations for the 2023 FIFA Women’s World Cup.
